title: P1-IIId public SFHo-18.8 profile and composition provenance audit

primary_source.citation: A. Caputo, G. Raffelt, and E. Vitagliano, Phys. Rev. D 105, 035022 (2022), arXiv:2109.03244v3, Fig. 1
primary_source.status: Primary baseline source; density curves must be extracted from exact vector paths before radial kernel use.

independent_public_density_source.citation: H. Esseili and G. D. Kribs, Phys. Rev. D 114, 016023 (2026), Fig. 12
independent_public_density_source.model: Includes SFHo-18.8 among four representative models
independent_public_density_source.status: Independent cross-check candidate; do not merge until T, n_p, and n_n+n_p versus Caputo n_B are compared.

alternative_composition_source.citation: Phenomenology of Light Particles on Earth and in the Sky, Fig. 8.1
alternative_composition_source.eos: SFHoY with hyperons, postprocessed using CompOSE
alternative_composition_source.status: Separate EOS-composition sensitivity diagnostic, not baseline SFHo composition.

physics_scope.current_kernel: free neutron and free proton scattering only
physics_scope.closure_warning: Do not infer n_n_free=n_B-n_p_free without species-definition and composition closure.

next_steps: Extract Caputo n_B,n_p,n_e vector paths with exact path indices and source vertices.
Digitize Esseili-Kribs Fig. 12 n_n,n_p,T and compare against Caputo over common radii.
Digitize SFHoY Y_n,Y_p,Y_Lambda separately as an EOS-variant sensitivity.
Establish a radial free-nucleon validity mask and quantify non-free baryon fractions.
Only then construct radial free-nucleon densities and integrate the P1-IIIb kernel.
